properties.Notes: This mapped area functions as an overlay rather than a standard base zoning district. Article IX permits only certain open-space uses by right within the special flood hazard area, including agriculture, recreation, and accessory residential open-space uses such as lawns, gardens, parking areas, and play areas. New construction, substantial improvement, and other development not meeting Section 906 require conditional use approval and must satisfy flood-specific review and construction standards. No standard district setback table is provided here, so dimensional fields should be treated as not applicable unless they are inherited from the underlying base district.

NC-1 allows one- and two-family dwellings, retail and service uses, community facilities, daycare under the by-right threshold, accessory apartments, and home occupations by right, while multifamily dwellings are conditional rather than permitted. The district standards are 1 acre minimum lot area, 100 feet minimum frontage, 75 feet front setback, 30 feet rear setback, 15 feet side setback, and 35 feet maximum building height. The bylaw also allows the Development Review Board to waive setback requirements as part of a conditional use application, so those setback values should be understood as the standard district values rather than absolute values in every approved case. Parking for multifamily dwellings is not separately broken out in the residential parking table, so any multifamily parking interpretation should be flagged for case-by-case review.

R-2 allows one- and two-family dwellings by right, with accessory apartments permitted under the general ADU provisions applicable in districts allowing single-family dwellings. The district standards are 2 acres minimum lot area, 200 feet minimum frontage, 90 feet front setback, 50 feet rear setback, 50 feet side setback, and 35 feet maximum building height. Front yard setback in Panton is defined using the distance from the building to the street line plus the distance from the street line to the centerline of the existing road, so the setback value should be understood using that definition rather than as a pure property-line setback. Planned Unit Development is a conditional use and should be tracked under PUD rather than PRD.

R-5 allows one- and two-family dwellings, accessory uses, home occupations, group or residential care homes, small daycare, and accessory apartments by right, while Planned Unit Development and several nonresidential uses are conditional. The district standards are 5 acres minimum lot area, 400 feet minimum frontage, 90 feet front setback, 50 feet rear setback, 50 feet side setback, and 35 feet maximum building height. Front yard setback in Panton is defined using the street line plus the road centerline distance, so the listed front setback should be read using that bylaw definition. Planned Unit Development is addressed through the townwide PUD provisions, and I did not find a separate PRD section in the bylaw.

RA-10 allows one- and two-family dwellings, accessory uses, home occupations, nurseries and greenhouses, group or residential care homes, small daycare, and accessory apartments by right, while campgrounds, community facilities, public utility buildings, residential health care facilities, Planned Unit Development, and larger daycare facilities are conditional. The district standards are 10 acres minimum lot area, 600 feet minimum frontage, 90 feet front setback, 50 feet rear setback, 50 feet side setback, and 35 feet maximum building height. Front yard setback in Panton is defined using the street line plus the road centerline distance, so the listed front setback should be interpreted using that bylaw definition. Planned Unit Development is recognized in the bylaw, but I did not find a separate PRD section.
